result:
I would eliminate the conceptual inability to comprehend long-term consequences. 

I would sever the biological and cognitive disconnect that makes the abstract future feel less real than the immediate present. 

If I could change the world, the year 2150 would carry as much psychological weight, urgency, and emotional reality as tomorrow does. The pain of a drought fifty years from now would instinctively register with the same sensory urgency as a burn on a hand today.

This would entirely rewire human motivation. The traps of short-term gratification—rampant resource extraction, compounding debt, political polarization, ecological destruction—would collapse, not out of moral awakening, but out of sheer, inescapable self-interest. The horizon would no longer feel like a place you never have to reach.
